paragraphs.notes: Continuation page inside the Patentansprueche: the claims open on printed page 79 (p81) and this page carries no claim number, no heading and no paragraph marker of its own, so marker is null. The whole page body is one unbroken enumeration of substituent group names, 34 printed lines, and it is recorded as a single paragraph. The page opens mid-word: the preceding page (printed 91, p93) ends with the hyphenated fragment 'Heteroarylalkylsulfonyl-N-', and the first token here, 'alkyl-amino,', completes it. The list is not finished at the foot of this page either; it runs on into printed page 93 (p95), which begins 'Halogenalkoxycarbonyl,'. The final printed character on this page is a comma, not a semicolon or full stop. Line-break hyphens have been closed up without a space where the hyphen belongs to the term itself ('N-alkyl-/amino' -> 'N-alkyl-amino', 'N-Alkyl-N-/arylaminocarbonyl' -> 'N-Alkyl-N-arylaminocarbonyl', 'N-Alkyl-N-/heteroarylaminocarbonyl' -> 'N-Alkyl-N-heteroarylaminocarbonyl'); the zh field is otherwise the printed text verbatim, run together as the single sentence it is. The zh field holds the verbatim German, per the convention this run uses for a German-language patent. German capitalisation of the nouns is kept in zh and dropped in en, matching the lower-case chemical-name style used on the earlier claim pages. The en field renders the Germanised chemical names into their English equivalents: Alkinyl -> alkynyl, Halogen- as a prefix -> halo-, 'gegebenenfalls substituiertes' -> 'optionally substituted'. Note that 'Halogen' here is the prefix meaning halo, not the element name; and that 'Alkinyl' is alkynyl, not alkenyl, a pair the scan sets only one letter apart and which was checked letter by letter on every occurrence. Two hyphenation styles appear side by side in the printed text and are preserved as printed: 'Alkylcarbonyl-N-arylamino' and 'Alkylcarbonyl-N-heteroarylamino' have no hyphen before 'amino', while 'Arylcarbonyl-N-alkyl-amino' and 'Heteroarylcarbonyl-N-alkyl-amino' do. There are no subscripts, superscripts, numerals or formula labels anywhere on the page. A small ink squiggle sits in the white gap between printed lines 3 and 4, above the '-N-alkyl-' of 'Heterocyclylalkylsulfonyl-N-alkyl-amino'; it touches no character and is a scan artifact, not a mark of the text. The same artifact recurs on the following page. A faint stray dot sits in the left margin level with the header line, and another in the left margin about two thirds down; both are outside the text block. The lower quarter of the page, below the last printed line, is blank, and the page carries no footer.
